requirements.quote:
The name server side of a security-aware recursive name server MUST
   NOT set the AD bit in a response unless the name server considers all
   RRsets in the Answer and Authority sections of the response to be
   authentic.  The name server side SHOULD set the AD bit if and only if
   the resolver side considers all RRsets in the Answer section and any
   relevant negative response RRs in the Authority section to be
   authentic.  The resolver side MUST follow the procedure described in
   Section 5 to determine whether the RRs in question are authentic.
   However, for backward compatibility, a recursive name server MAY set
   the AD bit when a response includes unsigned CNAME RRs if those CNAME




Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 18]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   RRs demonstrably could have been synthesized from an authentic DNAME
   RR that is also included in the response according to the synthesis
   rules described in [RFC2672].
requirements.condition: The name server side of a security-aware recursive name server generates a response and does not consider every RRset in its Answer and Authority sections authentic; the stated backward-compatibility exception permits unsigned CNAME RRs demonstrably synthesizable under RFC2672 from an authentic DNAME RR also included in the response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The name server side MUST NOT set the AD bit unless all such RRsets are considered authentic, subject to the stated unsigned-CNAME exception.
requirements.why_checkable: Inspect the AD-bit assignment guard and exercise responses with an RRset not considered authentic, accounting for the explicitly permitted synthesized-CNAME exception.

requirements.quote:
The name server side SHOULD set the AD bit if and only if
   the resolver side considers all RRsets in the Answer section and any
   relevant negative response RRs in the Authority section to be
   authentic.
requirements.condition: The resolver side of a security-aware recursive name server considers all RRsets in the Answer section and any relevant negative response RRs in the Authority section authentic.
requirements.required_behavior: The name server side SHOULD set the AD bit in the response.
requirements.why_checkable: Observe the recommended AD-bit value when all Answer RRsets and relevant negative Authority RRs have authentic validation results.

RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   RRs demonstrably could have been synthesized from an authentic DNAME

requirements.condition: The resolver side of a security-aware recursive name server does not consider all RRsets in the Answer section and any relevant negative response RRs in the Authority section authentic, outside the stated backward-compatibility exception for unsigned CNAME RRs demonstrably synthesizable from an authentic DNAME RR included in the response under RFC2672.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The name server side SHOULD NOT set the AD bit when the recommended authenticity condition is not satisfied, subject to the stated unsigned-CNAME exception.
requirements.why_checkable: The only-if direction of the SHOULD recommendation can be checked by observing AD when a relevant validation result is not authentic; its advisory strength is retained.

requirements.quote:
The resolver side MUST follow the procedure described in
   Section 5 to determine whether the RRs in question are authentic.
requirements.condition: The resolver side determines whether the RRs in question are authentic for the AD-bit decision.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver side MUST follow the procedure described in Section 5 to determine authenticity.
requirements.why_checkable: This identifies a mandatory validation procedure, but Section 5 is outside this isolated chunk, so its operational steps cannot be established from the available evidence.

requirements.quote:
The name server side of a security-aware recursive name server MUST
   NOT set the AD bit in a response unless the name server considers all
   RRsets in the Answer and Authority sections of the response to be
   authentic.  The name server side SHOULD set the AD bit if and only if
   the resolver side considers all RRsets in the Answer section and any
   relevant negative response RRs in the Authority section to be
   authentic.  The resolver side MUST follow the procedure described in
   Section 5 to determine whether the RRs in question are authentic.
   However, for backward compatibility, a recursive name server MAY set
   the AD bit when a response includes unsigned CNAME RRs if those CNAME




Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 18]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   RRs demonstrably could have been synthesized from an authentic DNAME
   RR that is also included in the response according to the synthesis

requirements.condition: For backward compatibility, a recursive name server generates a response containing unsigned CNAME RRs that demonstrably could have been synthesized, under the RFC2672 synthesis rules, from an authentic DNAME RR also included in the response; other applicable AD authenticity conditions remain satisfied.
requirements.required_behavior: The recursive name server MAY set the AD bit despite those CNAME RRs being unsigned.
requirements.why_checkable: The permitted AD-bit exception is conditioned on the unsigned CNAMEs being demonstrably synthesizable and the corresponding authentic DNAME being present; enabling this optional behavior is not mandatory.
